cause: The text says a small structure or feature on an organ is absent ('dots/glands/hairs/domatia/cystoliths/annulus/aril/peg absent', 'A without B', 'Hairs: absent' in an anatomy table, '<feature> over/on <organ> absent'). The absence is put on the organ that carries it: the subject of the clause, the section organ, or the noun after 'of/on/over'.
remedy: In flopo2/ingest/ncvc_annotate.py the absence path (around lines 2709-2732, grounding.negate) must treat absence_scope_problem() == 'absence_of_another_part' as a rebind, not a pass. The absent bearer is the head noun next to the cue: the last noun before _ABSENCE_AFTER, or the first noun after _ABSENCE_BEFORE. In 'Name: absent' lines it is the noun before the colon. The row's part (or section organ) becomes bearer_container/location only. If the head noun does not ground, emit nothing and never fall back to the organ. Add lexicon/bearer rows for nouns that do have a class: hairs/trichomes -> trichome PO:0000282; gland -> PO:0005656; domatium FLOPO_0986021; colleter FLOPO_0986023; marginal/intramarginal/collective vein -> PO_0025520; aril PO:0009090; bulbil FLOPO:0986055; leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106. Nouns with no class (cystolith, flap, apical peg, annulus, syrinx, soredia, crystals, tannins) give no row. Add to the transcription prompt: 'In "<feature> absent" or "without <feature>", the part is the feature; the organ being described goes in the whole/container field.'
detectable: yes: absence_scope_problem() already returns 'absence_of_another_part' for these spans. Also flag a PATO_0000462 row whose bearer label/synonyms are not the head noun next to the absence cue, or whose bearer has positive qualities in the same taxon.
example: 'Leaves ... dots absent' and 'cystoliths absent' were recorded as leaf lamina absent; 'Hairs: absent' under Fruit was recorded as fruit absent.

cause: The text denies only one kind, position, sex or order of a part (cauline/basal leaves, lower glume, ray/disc florets, phyllodia, rudimentary ovary, involucral or lateral bracts, sterile flowers, secondary branches, marginal vein). The modifier is dropped and the absence goes on the general parent class, which contradicts the members that are described.
remedy: Before any PATO_0000462 is written, ground the whole noun phrase (modifier + head) against po_lexicon, longest match first, and never fall back to the head noun. Phrase rows: cauline/stem leaves -> cauline leaf PO_0000013; basal/radical leaves, basal rosette -> rosette leaf PO_0000014 / rosette PO:0025615; lower/first glume -> PO_0006002; upper/second glume -> PO_0006004; ray florets/eradiate -> PO_0025331; disc florets -> PO_0025332; phyllodia -> PO_0025335; rudimentary/vestigial ovary, pistillode -> PO_0009078; involucral bracts/phyllaries -> PO:0009045; bracteole -> PO_0009043; calyculus/ecalyculate -> epicalyx PO:0009063; pistillate/staminate flowers -> PO:0025599/PO:0025600. If no class matches, keep the modifier as a context slot from config/flora_context_words.tsv (sterile PATO:0000956, lateral, outer, axillary, basal FLOPO:0991002). If neither works, hold the row. Make the 'absence_of_a_kind_of_the_part' and 'absence_in_some_members' results of absence_scope_problem() hard holds on every path, including the reviewed-rule negation path that skips the check today (grounding.negate).
detectable: yes: an absence row whose source span has a modifier before or after the part noun that the bearer label lacks (absence_scope_problem() returns 'absence_of_a_kind_of_the_part' or 'absence_in_some_members'), or an absent class that is an ancestor of a class described as present in the same taxon.
example: 'Cauline leaves absent' became leaf PO:0025034 absent, and 'lower glume absent' became glume absent, although the upper glume is described.

cause: A note that material was missing ('not seen', 'not known', 'unknown', 'not observed', 'not collected', 'non vu(e)s', 'inconnu(e)s', 'caducous, not seen') is recorded as the part being absent (PATO_0000462), and sometimes also as present or on a nearby part.
remedy: Extend _NOT_OBSERVED (ncvc_annotate.py:568) with 'not collected', 'not yet collected', 'not visible' after a colon, 'non observé\w*', 'pas connu\w*', 'non connu\w*', 'ignot\w*', 'imperfectly known', 'known only from', 'absent\?', 'possibly absent'. Test it on the whole clause, for every row and for every noun of a coordinated subject ('A, B and C not seen'), before any grounding and outside absence_scope_problem(). Then drop the row: no absent, no present, and no quality on that part from the same clause. If the clause also says 'caducous'/'early deciduous', keep only that (fugacious FLOPO:0991231). Re-annotate all rows made before 2026-11-15. Transcription prompt: '<part> not seen / not known / unknown / not observed / non vu / inconnu reports missing material. Write no row for it, never absent.'
detectable: yes: _NOT_OBSERVED (plus the added words) matches the source span of a PATO_0000462 or PATO_0000467 row.
example: 'Flowers not known; fruit not seen' became flower absent and fruit absent.

cause: A privative word said of one axis or member ('leafless stem/scape/branch', 'leafless except at apex', '<peduncle> ebracteate', 'awnless/muticous glume', 'veinless septum', 'stemless') becomes a taxon-wide absence of leaves, bracts, awns, veins or stem.
remedy: A privative (-less, e-...-ate, a-, 'without', 'muticous', 'dépourvu de') with a subject noun gives the denied part absent with that subject as bearer_container, or a subject-specific class. 'leafless' after stem/scape/culm/peduncle/branch/flowering stem -> cauline leaf PO_0000013 absent on that axis. '<axis> ebracteate' -> bract part_of that axis absent; in Asteraceae never involucral bract absent. 'awnless/muticous' on glume/lemma/palea -> glume awn PO_0025351 / lemma awn PO_0006032 / palea awn PO_0025350 absent. 'veinless/not veined <part>' -> vein part_of that part. 'leafless except/only at X', 'leafless below/in lower part' -> leaves limited to X, no absence. 'stemless/acaulescent' -> whole plant acaulescent FLOPO_0980080, never stem absent. Use whole-plant leaf absence only when the plant is the subject and no leaf is described. Check: no taxon-level absence of a part that has positive rows in the same taxon.
detectable: yes: an absence of leaf, bract, awn, vein or stem whose span holds a privative word next to a different subject noun (stem, scape, peduncle, glume, sheath), or 'except/below/only', while the taxon has positive rows for the denied part.
example: 'Scapes leafless' became leaf absent for a rosette plant whose basal leaves are described.

cause: A part word whose meaning depends on the family or the section is grounded with its general PO sense: grass/bamboo auricle, oral setae and culm sheath -> stipule; Carex utricle/perigynium -> fruit; moss capsule -> fruit; Apiaceae/Cyperaceae rays -> ray flower or bract; orchid spur/lip; Asteraceae ligule; cactus spines -> thorn; tepals -> petal.
remedy: Add a family-scoped bearer table (family or flora group, word, PO class) that the annotator checks before config/po_lexicon.tsv. Poaceae/bamboos: auricle -> leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106; culm sheath -> leaf sheath PO_0020104; oral setae -> trichome PO:0000282 at the sheath mouth; stipule PO_0020041 blocked as a bearer. Cyperaceae: utricle/perigynium -> PO_0009044; spikelet scales -> floral bract; rays -> inflorescence branch PO_0009081. Apiaceae: rays -> umbel ray (inflorescence branch); bracts -> involucral bract; bracteoles -> bracteole PO_0009043. Bryophyta: capsule -> sporangium PO_0025094; leaves -> non-vascular leaf PO_0025075; teeth -> peristome tooth PO_0030043; costa only in mosses. Orchidaceae: lip -> labellum; spur -> floral spur, never short shoot PO_0004701. Asteraceae: ligule -> ray-flower corolla, not PO_0020105. Cactaceae: spine -> spine leaf PO_0025173. Monocots/Lauraceae: tepals, perianth segments -> tepal PO_0009033. Old grass floras: first/second/third/fourth scale -> lower glume / upper glume / sterile lemma / fertile lemma. Hold an ambiguous word with no row for that family.
detectable: yes: join the taxon family to (word, bearer) and flag blocked pairs, for example stipule in Poaceae, fruit from 'utricle' in Cyperaceae, a fruit class in a moss, ray flower in Apiaceae, short shoot inside a flower clause.
example: Bamboo 'auricles and oral setae absent' became stipule absent.

cause: A region word that opens or closes the clause ('apex acute', 'base cuneate to rounded', 'X at the apex', 'margin entire', 'tip', 'lobes ...', 'tube ...') does not narrow the bearer, so the quality goes on the whole organ. This happens most often with alternatives, continua and relation paths.
remedy: Make plan_bearer_scope() (ncvc_annotate.py:457) run on every path: single values, unions, continua, negations and relations (pattern 09/10). It should fire when the span starts with apex/apices/tip/base/margin/border/limb/tube/lobes, or contains 'at (the) apex/base', 'au sommet', 'à la base', 'from a <shape> base', 'with a <colour> tip'. A trailing place phrase covers every alternative before it. Substitute the region class of the current organ: leaf apex PO:0020137, leaf base PO:0020040, leaf lamina base PO:0008019, the organ's margin, corolla tube FLOPO_0985018, corolla lobe FLOPO_0986006, calyx lobe FLOPO_0986005. With no PO region class, use the BSPO apical/basal region as part_restrictions. Strip the region word from the value text before matching, so 'apex rounded' does not hit 'more rounded' FLOPO_0980236. In 'adnate/inserted at base of X', X is the target and base its region. Transcription prompt: 'If a quality is said of a place on the part (apex, base, margin, tip, tube, lobes), write that place as the part.'
detectable: yes: the span starts with, or contains, apex|base|tip|margin|tube|lobes|at the apex|at base, but the bearer is the whole organ and the scope slot is empty. Apex-only or base-only terms (acuminate, cordate, cuneate) on a whole lamina are also suspect.
example: 'Leaflets ..., base cuneate to rounded' gave cuneate to the whole leaflet.

cause: A lexicon synonym, stem match or fuzzy match grounds a part word to a broader or wrong PO class: caudex/scape/culm/trunk -> stem; stipel/stipelle -> stipule; bracteole/bractlet -> bract; peduncle -> pedicel; staminode/filament -> stamen; vein -> vascular bundle; perigynium -> involucral bract; pyrene -> seed; rootstock -> root. An absence through such a synonym then denies the broad class.
remedy: config/po_lexicon.tsv: remove caudex|caudices|scape|culm|trunk|cane|primocane|stalk from stem PO_0009047, or mark them narrow and block them in absences (scape -> peduncle PO:0009053). Remove 'vein' from vascular bundle PO_0005020 and map leaf veins to leaf lamina vein PO_0020138, secondary leaf vein PO_0020140 ('N on each side of midrib'), PO_0025520 (intramarginal). Remove 'bractlet' from PO_0009043 duplicates on bract, and 'perigynium' from involucral bract PO_0009045. Add exact rows: stipel/stipels/stipelle(s)/stipellate/estipellate -> PO_0020051; staminode -> PO_0009077; filament -> PO_0009067; infructescence -> PO_0006342; pyrene/stone -> endocarp; albumen -> endosperm PO_0009089; tepal -> PO_0009033; standard/vexillum -> banner petal PO_0025324. Annotator: match whole words, longest first; turn off suffix-stripped and fuzzy part matching (stipel never reaches stipule); never write an absence that was reached through a narrow synonym. Add a lint that flags any synonym listed on two classes.
detectable: yes: the source noun is not the label or an exact synonym of the grounded class (only a stem, fuzzy or narrow-synonym match), for example 'stipel' -> stipule, 'caudex' -> stem absent, 'peduncle' -> pedicel.
example: 'Stipels absent' became stipule absent; 'caudex absent' became stem absent.

cause: Bounds, extremes and number formats are misparsed: 'to ±', 'to c.', 'may/can reach', 'reaching/atteignant/jusqu'à', 'to more than', 'at least', 'N or more/less', '(to N)' in brackets, '× to W', 'N(M)', '(N or)M', '--', fractions ½ and the inch/foot marks, 'mm.' with a full stop, OCR '|' for 1, 'd.b.h.', and rows held before dm conversion.
remedy: Before parsing, normalise the text: '--' and en dash -> '-'; ½ ¼ ¾ -> decimals; ′/' -> ft and ″/" -> in (keep source_unit); 'mm.'/'cm.'/'dm.' -> unit; a lone '|' or 'l' next to digits -> 1; strip U+00AD. In gates.UPPER_BOUND_EVIDENCE (flopo2/verify/gates.py:70) and normalize_bounds() (ncvc_annotate.py:1807): allow ±/c./ca./~ between 'to' and the number (value_qualifier approximately); allow a cue inside brackets; a bare 'to/up to/reaching/atteignant/jusqu'à/may reach/can reach/grows to' gives value_high only, never N-N; 'to' after '×' bounds the second dimension; 'to more than/exceeding' is a strict lower bound and is tested before 'to'; 'at least', 'N or more', 'N+', 'ou plus' give a lower bound; 'N or less/shorter' gives an inclusive upper bound and is never an 'or' list; 'N(M)', '(N or)M', 'M(or K)', 'rarely/occasionally up to M' give extremes (pattern 05). 'd.b.h.' -> diameter PATO:0001334 of the stem. Re-annotate every row held for a unit (dm, ft, in) since 2026-11-15.
detectable: yes: a regex on the source span for these cues and symbols on rows that were held, or whose value_low equals value_high while the span has 'to'.
example: 'Shrub to ± 3 m' was held; 'petiole to 2 cm' was stored as 2-2 cm.

cause: A word that limits the statement to some members of a series is dropped (lower/upper/lowest, inner/outer, lateral/dorsal/median, proximal/distal ones, basal vs cauline/stem leaves, 'the N inner'), so a value for one set is given to every member and contradicts the others.
remedy: Transcription prompt: 'Copy every word that picks out some members of a part (upper, lower, lowest, uppermost, inner, outer, lateral, median, dorsal, proximal, distal, basal, cauline, stem leaves, the outer ones, the lowest 2) into the position field of every row it governs, until a new part is named. Resolve "ones", "the inner", "the lower" to the noun they replace. "the outer X, the inner Y" gives one row per position.' Annotator: fill the pattern-04 position slot from config/flora_context_words.tsv: upper FLOPO:0991376, lower FLOPO:0991377, median FLOPO:0991381, lateral FLOPO:0991380, inner FLOPO:0991378, outer FLOPO:0991379, basal FLOPO:0991002, cauline FLOPO:0991117. Add missing rows: dorsal, ventral, lowermost, distalmost, middle pairs, internes/externes, supérieur(e)s/inférieur(e)s. Hold a row whose source has an unused position word.
detectable: yes: the span or the clause opener has a position word from flora_context_words.tsv but the position slot is empty, or the same taxon, bearer and attribute have conflicting values with no position.
example: 'Outer sepals ovate, inner ones lanceolate' gave sepal both ovate and lanceolate.

cause: The quality is bound to the organ at the head of the sentence, or to a part from an earlier clause, instead of the nearest part noun the words describe (filaments, internodes, claw, segments, glomerules, the noun after 'with', the subject of a parenthesis, an appositive, the latter part).
remedy: Transcription prompt: 'The part of a row is the nearest noun that the value describes, in the same comma or semicolon clause: the sub-part named (tube, lobes, filament, claw, internodes, segments, veins, spur, margins), the noun after "with", the subject of a parenthesis, or a new subject after a semicolon. Write the larger organ as the whole. A clause keeps the last part named until a new part is named. A part just said to be absent is never the bearer of the next quality. When one quality follows a list of parts, write one row per part.' Annotator: if the span holds a PO-lexicon noun that is part_of the grounded bearer and stands before the value, rebind to it with the bearer as container. Hold a quality whose bearer has an absence row from the same sentence.
detectable: partly: the span holds a PO-lexicon noun, other than the bearer or its synonyms, between the bearer word and the value, or the bearer is an ancestor of that noun.
example: 'Stamens 10, filaments 3-5 mm' gave the length to stamen.

cause: A quality word is grounded to the wrong value: glaucous -> green, compressed -> condensed, fuscous -> red, tan -> orange, rounded -> 'more rounded' or obtuse, apiculate -> the attribute sharpness, splitting -> split, confluent -> connate, tomentose -> 'pubescent hair', a 2-D shape on a solid organ, or a process verb ('opening widely', 'enlarging in fruit') not mapped to its state.
remedy: config/pato_lexicon.tsv and the colour and value tables: glaucous/glaucescent/pruinose -> glaucous PATO_0104277 (remove the green FLOPO_0988006 rows in botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv; 'not glaucous' negates PATO_0104277); move 'compressed' from condensed PATO_0001485 to flattened PATO_0002254 / laterally compressed PATO_0002054; fuscous -> dark greyish brown; tan -> light brown; straw-colored/stramineous -> straw yellow PATO_0104343; plain 'rounded' -> obtuse only on an apex or base, spherical on solids, never FLOPO_0980236; apiculate -> a value class, never PATO_0000944; tomentose -> PATO_0002341 and pubescent -> PATO_0000455, never 'pubescent hair' PATO_0001320 on an organ; splitting/opening of a fruit -> dehiscent FLOPO:0991149; confluent/fused with another part -> adnate FLOPO:0991129 with towards; enlarging in fruit -> accrescent FLOPO:0991082; opening widely -> open PATO:0000610; climbing words handled separately. In '<modifier> <colour>' and 'Xish Y' the last colour is the head. Add a check that never emits a bare attribute class as a value.
detectable: yes: a fixed list of source words (glauc*, compressed, fuscous, tan, rounded, apiculate, splitting, confluent, tomentose) compared with their reviewed target, and value rows whose quality is an attribute class.
example: 'Leaves glaucous beneath' became leaf approximately green.

cause: Words that put the quality on one side or surface of the part (adaxially/abaxially, above/beneath, upper/lower surface, inside/outside, on the veins, en dessus/en dessous, between the nerves) are dropped, or not carried across a list or a 'then' clause, so the quality covers the whole part.
remedy: Add or extend rows in config/flora_context_words.tsv: above/adaxially/upper surface/face supérieure/en dessus -> adaxial surface; beneath/below/abaxially/lower surface/face inférieure/en dessous -> abaxial surface; inside/within/à l'intérieur -> inner surface; outside/à l'extérieur -> outer surface; on (the) veins/nerves, in vein axils, between the nerves -> vein region. Annotator: read these words whether they come before or after the value. Apply them to every alternative and every value in the comma run up to the next side word or semicolon, and across 'puis/then'. 'X abaxially, Y adaxially' gives each value its own side. On a non-flat organ (stipe, stem, perigynium), above/below means distal/proximal region. Hold the row if the slot cannot be filled. Transcription prompt: 'Copy side and surface words into the place field of the row they limit.'
detectable: yes: the span holds a side/surface word from the table but the record has no surface or region slot and the bearer is the whole organ.
example: 'Lamina glabrous above, pubescent on veins beneath' gave lamina both glabrous and pubescent.

cause: Cue wordings are missing for count patterns that already exist: count per position or per unit ('per node', 'per (leaf-)axil', 'in each furrow', 'per cell/locule', 'per segment', 'each containing N', 'each bearing N', 'on each side', 'in whorls of N', 'N pairs'), and general cue phrases (frequency, relation).
remedy: Add count_position rows (pattern 14, used by count_position(), ncvc_annotate.py:1060): per_node 'per node', 'at each node', 'in whorls of N' (also emits whorled PATO:0001951), 'nodes with N'; per_axil 'per leaf-axil', 'in each leaf axil', 'to each axil' (landmark leaf axil PO:0009023); each_side 'on each side (of midrib)', 'on each margin', 'per side', 'at either side'; at_region 'in each furrow' (landmark canal PO:0025132), 'on commissure', 'at apex/tips'; per_locule 'per cell/locule', 'in each cell', 'each containing N' (landmark locule PO:0025263); per_branch 'per (ultimate) branch' (PO:0025073); per_segment 'per segment'; per_turn 'per cycle of spiral'; 'N pairs (of)' -> count with collection size 2 (as -jugate). Add the cue words 'commonly', 'less often', 'covered by' (surrounded by PATO:0005016), 'behind' (proximal to PATO:0001195). Look for the cue anywhere in the counted noun's own clause, not only in the transcribed span.
detectable: yes: held count rows whose source contains per|each|in each|on each|whorls of|pairs next to a number, with no count_position; and a report of the frequent unmatched n-grams in held rows.
example: 'Flowers 2-4 per leaf-axil' was held because 'leaf-axil' with a hyphen is not a cue.

cause: A count written inside a word ('3-5-lobed', '1–3-nerved', '4(-6)-angled', '2- or 3-branched', '1 -awned', 'palmately 3-lobed', 'N-M-seeded') is not split. Causes are an en dash, a suspended hyphen, a bracketed extreme, an adverb in front, a place word, or the split running after the unit check. The row is then held as a measurement without a unit or sent to count_per_position.
remedy: In counts_from_compounds() (ncvc_annotate.py:953), run before the measurement and unit checks: normalise en/em dash, '--' and a space before the hyphen; accept 'N', 'N-M', 'N(-M)', '(N-)M', 'N(or M)', 'N- or M-<suffix>' (range N-M) and number words; strip a leading degree or manner adverb (shallowly, palmately, obscurely, unequally) and keep it as a cue. A count never gets a missing-length-unit hold (unit = count). The container is the clause subject (the organ before 'N-<suffix>ed'). 'margin', 'apex' or 'at base' next to the word is a region of the counted part, never a count_per_position trigger; use count_per_position only with a real pattern-14 cue in the counted noun's clause. 'in N rows/series' and 'N-seriate' count rows (uniseriate FLOPO:0991090, biseriate FLOPO:0991089), not parts. A count of 0 means the part is absent.
detectable: yes: rows held as 'measurement_missing_unit' or count_per_position whose span matches \d+(\(?[-–]\d+\)?)*\s*-\s*[a-zé]+(ed|ate|é)\b.
example: 'Calyx 4–5(–6)-lobed' was held as a number without a unit.

cause: A count gets no container, or the wrong one: the counted part itself, its is_a parent (vein -> vascular bundle), the whole plant, or a landmark (midvein, axil). The container that is meant is the clause subject or the named unit ('Racemes 10-flowered', 'each X contains', Asteraceae 'Florets N' per head, 'N per X'), and sometimes the place phrase was transcribed as the part.
remedy: In count_container() (ncvc_annotate.py:846), choose the container in this order: the noun after 'per/each/in each/chaque/par'; the subject before 'each containing/bearing'; the organ that 'N-flowered/-seeded/-veined' is said of; the organ at the head of the semicolon run or section heading ('Ray florets:', 'Fruit', the involucre -> capitulum PO_0030121 for florets in Asteraceae). Reject a container that equals or subsumes the counted part (vascular bundle PO_0005020 for veins), and put landmarks (midvein, axil) in count_position. Ground container words: cell in ovary/fruit -> locule PO_0025263; segment -> leaf lamina lobe PO_0025517 or fruit valve PO:0000033; first/second scale -> PO_0006002/PO_0006004; cincinni -> PO_0030132; bare rachis in an inflorescence -> PO_0020122. Transcription prompt: 'In "N per X" the counted thing is the part and X the container; never write "per X" as the part.'
detectable: yes: a count row whose container is empty, equals or subsumes the bearer, is whole plant while the clause subject is an organ, or whose part text starts with per/each/in.
example: 'Veins 6-8 on each side of midrib' got vascular bundle as its container.

cause: Lists of alternatives and ranges are scoped or split wrongly: an 'or' blocks or takes in values from other comma clauses; 'A to B or C' loses A or C; 'and' is read as 'or'; ', rarely Y', 'and/or' and '(or X)' are not read as alternatives; 'X or subX', 'X or nearly so' and 'several or many' are sent to the union check; the first member of 'A, B or C' is dropped.
remedy: Parse the value list as a tree. Split the clause at commas and semicolons first, and test for a disjunction (gates.unexplained_disjunction) only inside the comma item that holds 'or/ou/and/or'. Inside that item, 'or' and ', rarely/occasionally/sometimes Y' make union operands (pattern 07/08), each with its own frequency; 'to' makes a continuum; 'A to B or C' = continuum(A,B) ∪ C. A comma list with no 'or' or 'to' gives one record per value (and). 'X or nearly/almost/broadly so', 'X or subX' and 'X or <narrower form of X>' give X approximately. 'several or many' and 'N or N+1' are one count range. An 'or' inside 'with ... hairs' or 'in form of ...' only modifies that noun. Collapse a union whose operands ground to the same class. Every source value word must reach an operand or a flag. Add the reviewed pairs reported as missing (linear | dilated, entire | lobed, pink | rose, caespitose | pulvinate, paired | bifurcate, climbing | procumbent) to config/flora_union_pairs.tsv.
detectable: yes: compare the value words in the span (split on or/to/,/à) with the grounded operands; also flag held disjunctions whose 'or' lies outside the value's comma item, and spans that start with 'or'.
example: 'Leaves glabrous, margins ciliate or not' held 'glabrous' because the 'or' was in another comma clause.

cause: A hedged or weakened statement ('nearly/almost/practically/seemingly leafless', 'subaphyllous', '± absent', 'without distinct/significant/well-developed X', 'not visible/evident', 'obscure', 'not very X', 'not conspicuously X') is recorded as plain absence or full negation.
remedy: Gate on NEGATION_EVIDENCE (gates.py:55) and the absence path: when a hedge (nearly, almost, practically, essentially, virtually, apparently, seemingly, ±, sub-, subaphyllous, obsolete) comes before or is part of an absence word, never emit PATO_0000462. Record decreased amount PATO_0001997 or vestigial PATO_0000588 on the named axis, scale leaf PO:0006003 when scale leaves are named, or nothing. 'without distinct/conspicuous/evident X', 'X not visible/evident', 'obscure', 'indistinct' -> inconspicuous PATO_0000464 on X. 'without significant/well-developed X', 'rudimentary' -> decreased size. 'not very/conspicuously/strongly/markedly X' -> X with a weak degree, or no row; never not-X.
detectable: yes: an absent or negated row whose span has a hedge word or a degree/visibility word (distinct, evident, visible, obscure, very, conspicuously, significant) next to the negation.
example: 'Stems nearly leafless' became leaf absent.

cause: A section heading or opening phrase that names a sex, flower type, morph or frond type ('Male flowers:', 'Fleurs ♀', 'Pistillate inflorescences', 'Ray florets ...;', 'Fertile fronds:', 'Pin flowers') is not carried to the rows below it, so a value for one kind is given to all.
remedy: Transcription prompt: 'A heading or lead-in naming a sex (male, female, staminate, pistillate, ♂, ♀), flower or floret type (ray, disc, cleistogamous, pin, thrum) or frond type (fertile, sterile) applies to every row until the next heading. Write it in the whole/state field of each row.' Annotator: keep a per-description heading stack. Fill bearer_whole with staminate flower PO_0025600 / pistillate flower PO_0025599 (or the sex PATO:0000384 / PATO:0000383 as state), ray flower PO_0025331, disk flower PO_0025332. Read sex words as pattern 12 (part_of a sexed flower), never as a stage. Add ♂, ♀, 'Plantule:', 'short-/long-stamened flowers' to config/flora_context_words.tsv.
detectable: yes: the description has a sex, floret-type or frond-type heading, but rows after it have an empty whole/state slot, or the same bearer has conflicting values under different headings.
example: 'Male flowers: sepals 4 ... Female flowers: sepals 5' gave sepal counts 4 and 5 to every flower.

cause: Comparisons and ratios with another part are not parsed: fractions ('1/3 length of blade', 'one-fourth as wide as', '0.3 the diameter of'), 'N × as long as', 'N length of X', 'similar to X but smaller', degree words before 'than', elliptical or plural targets, a shared target in coordinated comparatives, 'paler/darker than', and 'inserted at base of X' keeping only 'base'.
remedy: Extend comparison() (ncvc_annotate.py:321). Read fractions (n/m, word fractions half/one-third/two-thirds/three-quarters, ranges of fractions) and '× as long as' as ratio_low/ratio_high towards the named part (pattern 10), never as an absolute unit or a count. Add 'N length of X' (GrassBase), 'X-Y ratio a-b', 'N times as long as wide' (pattern 11), 'similar to X but smaller/larger', 'paler/darker than' (brightness/saturation towards X), 'exserted from/beyond X' (PATO:0000623), 'enveloped in/by' (PATO:0005016), 'articulated with' (PATO:0002278), 'surrounding X'. Allow degree words (slightly, much) before 'than' as RDF degrees. Spread one 'than X' over comparatives joined by 'and/but'. Lemmatise plural targets and resolve 'the tube', 'outer', 'ones' to the clause subject. In 'at/to the base/apex of X' the target is X with base/apex as its region. 'sub-' or 'about' before equal gives approximately, never exactly 1.0.
detectable: yes: the span has than|as long as|× as|times|the (length|width) of|a fraction, but the row has no towards target or carries a length unit not in the span.
example: 'Ligule 1/3 the length of the sheath' was held as a number with no unit.

cause: A quality of the hairs (colour, length, direction, density, shape) is put on the organ that carries them ('ferruginous tomentose', 'with yellowish hairs', 'hairs 0.5 mm long'), or 'hairs' is written in the quality slot.
remedy: Transcription prompt: 'Hairs, bristles, setae, scales, glands and prickles are parts, never qualities. In "<organ> with hairs N mm", "hairs white", "<colour> villous" the part is the hairs, with the organ as its whole; the organ's hairiness (villous, pubescent, glabrous) is a separate row on the organ.' Annotator: when the quality text is hair(s)/trichome(s)/setae with a number, move it to bearer trichome PO:0000282 with the old bearer as container and quality length PATO:0000122. When a colour or shape word comes just before, or hyphened to, an indumentum word (pubescent, villous, tomentose, tomentellous, hirsute, puberulent, hairy), or after 'with <colour> hairs', emit the colour on trichome PO:0000282 and the indumentum on the organ.
detectable: yes: the quality text is hair(s)/trichomes/setae, or a colour/length row on a non-trichome bearer whose span holds a hair word next to the value.
example: 'Twigs ferruginous-tomentose' gave the colour ferruginous to the twig.

cause: A hyphenated compound value ('oblong-lanceolate', 'ovate-elliptic', 'golden-yellow', 'obtuse-apiculate', 'lyrate-trifid') is read as a range, cut to one half, or blocks a union. Ranges with a compound end ('X to X-Y', 'A-B to C') lose their other end.
remedy: Tokenise hyphenated value words before splitting on 'to'/'or': only ' to ', '–' between whole words and 'or' are value separators. Look up the whole compound first (and its spaced form). If there is no term, read 'shape-shape' as one intermediate value (head = last word, first word = tendency, approximately), allowed as a union operand or a continuum end. Read 'outline-apex' compounds (ovate-acuminate, rhombic-acute, obtuse-apiculate) as outline on the lamina + apex shape at the apex. Read colour compounds 'X-Y' and 'Xish Y' with Y as head colour, with no 'approximately'. Read 'shape-auriculate', '-rostrate' as an extra part. Never keep only one half. Collapse a range whose ends ground to one class into one value.
detectable: yes: the span holds a hyphenated pair of lexicon words, but the row has only one of them, or a range whose two ends are the halves of one token.
example: 'Leaves oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate' became oblong to lanceolate.

cause: A word is grounded to a PATO process or direction quality on a plant structure (persistent PATO_0000082, continuous PATO_0000689, interrupted PATO_0000690, up/down, arrested, frequency, rate, precocious), which makes the class unsatisfiable.
remedy: Remap rows: persistent/persistant(e)s/not separating -> non-deciduous (any body part) PATO_0001732 (or marcescent FLOPO:0991181 where meant); caducous/caduc(ue)s -> fugacious FLOPO:0991231; interrupted/interrompu/intermittent/discontinuous on a structure -> structurally discontinuous PATO_0040026; 'continuous with' -> adnate FLOPO:0991129 or fused with PATO:0000642, otherwise drop; pointing/directed upward -> erect PATO_0000622 (ascending PATO_0104355 if oblique, antrorse PATO_0002238 on hairs); directed downward -> descending FLOPO:0991207 (retrorse PATO_0002237 on hairs); arrested -> abortive FLOPO_0991250; frequent/often/sporadic -> frequency qualifier, never PATO_0000044; short-lived/ephemeral -> decreased life span PATO_0001604; precocious, slow-growing, diurnal -> hold or route to a process bearer. Annotator check before output: reject any quality under PATO process quality on a PO/FLOPO anatomy bearer.
detectable: yes: the quality is a subclass of process quality in quality.obo with an anatomical bearer, or the ELK unsat list from DeprecateDumbClasses.
example: 'Calyx persistent' grounded to persistence PATO_0000082 and became unsatisfiable.

cause: A negation carried inside the word or in an uncommon form is not recognised: the prefixes e-/ex-/a-/in-/non- (eglandular, exstipulate, acaulescent, indehiscent, nonglandular), the suffix -less, 'neither ... nor', 'wanting', a postposed 'none', a count of '0', 'instead of', French 'nul'. The negation check then fails, or the positive value is emitted.
remedy: Extend NEGATION_EVIDENCE (flopo2/verify/gates.py:55) and the negated-value rules so that a reviewed privative word is its own cue (the whole word is the cue span). Use a reviewed list, not a free prefix rule, to spare words like 'elliptic': eglandular -> glandular PATO_0002117 negated; eciliate -> ciliate negated; epunctate -> punctate PATO_0001512 negated; ecarinate -> keel-shaped PATO_0002522 negated; exstipulate -> stipule absent; ebracteolate -> bracteole PO_0009043 absent; exalbuminous -> endosperm absent; indehiscent -> dehiscent negated; acaulescent -> FLOPO_0980080; '<noun>less' -> that noun absent; 'non-' prefix -> negated value; 'non-stipitate' -> sessile. Add 'neither X nor Y' (each negated), 'wanting', 'lacking', postposed 'none', '<part> 0' and 'nul/nulle(s)' as cues. Never emit the positive value when the span holds a negation cue. Flip polarity when grounding goes through an antonym.
detectable: yes: rows held for 'no negation cue' whose word matches the privative list or e-/ex-/non-/-less forms, and positive rows whose span holds not/neither/none/0/wanting.
example: 'Leaves eglandular' was held because the span has no separate negation word.

cause: The quality or part slot holds the wrong kind of thing: an attribute name ('shape', 'colour', 'number', 'texture') instead of the value word in the text; a part noun ('hairs', 'pulp', 'utricle') as the quality; a verb ('covered'); or a plain value rewritten as a negated opposite ('glabrous' as 'not pubescent').
remedy: Transcription prompt: 'The quality field holds the value word exactly as written (conical, glabrous, light-green, papery). Use an attribute (length, width, thickness) only when the text gives a number. Never write an attribute name without a number, a part noun, or a verb in the quality field. Do not rename or invert a value. "covered with scales" gives scales present (scaly PATO_0001804) plus rows on the scales.' Annotator check: hold a row whose quality grounds to a PO class or to an attribute_slim term with no number. If the span holds a value_slim label, use that value instead.
detectable: yes: the quality text matches config/po_lexicon.tsv, or grounds to attribute_slim without a number while the span holds a value term, or is negated with no negation word in the span.
example: 'Fruit globose' was transcribed with quality 'shape' and held as a measurement without a unit.

cause: Indefinite count words ('many', 'numerous', 'several', 'few', 'nombreux', '∞', 'containing many X', 'few to many', 'N-several') after or before a part, as a predicate, or with the transcribed quality 'number', are sent to the numeric measurement path or lose one end.
remedy: In indefinite_counts() (ncvc_annotate.py:1009), run before the numeric parser and send these to pattern 13 (part present PATO:0000467 + count_word, container from the clause): any row whose value or span holds a word of INDEFINITE_AMOUNTS, whatever the transcribed quality ('number', 'amount', empty). Accept the word before or after the noun, as a predicate ('X are numerous'), after 'containing/bearing/with', inside a comma list, and with an intensifier (very, assez, ±). Add nombreux/nombreuses, peu nombreux, '∞', 'single' (=1). Read 'few to many', 'several-many', 'pauci- à multi-' as count-word ranges and 'N-several/N-many' as a lower bound N with an open end. 'not many-flowered' gives 'few' (RDF).
detectable: yes: a row whose quality is 'number' with no digits, or whose span holds an INDEFINITE_AMOUNTS word, that was held or sent to the measurement path.
example: 'Stamens numerous' was held as a count with no number.

cause: A dimension word after a number ('2-4 mm thick', 'épais de 1 mm', 'N cm broad/wide/across', 'in diameter') is grounded as a value (thick, broad, increased thickness) instead of the measured attribute. Plant size is also misread: FNA 'a × b dm' as length, a bare stem size as height, 'spreading to N' as height.
remedy: Add a dimension-word table and use it before value grounding: after number + unit, thick/épais(se) de -> thickness PATO_0000915 (diameter PATO_0001334 for terete axes); broad/wide/large de/across -> width PATO_0000921; long/long(ue) de -> length PATO_0000122; tall/high -> height PATO_0000119; diam./in diameter -> diameter PATO_0001334. Never ground these to increased thickness PATO:0000591 or a value class when a number is present. For a whole plant or mat, 'A × B unit' is height × width. A bare 'Stems N cm', or the size of a decumbent, prostrate or climbing stem, is length; use height only for the whole plant or with tall/high. 'spreading N' is spread (width).
detectable: yes: a row with a numeric value and unit whose quality is a value class (thick, broad, increased X), or a height row whose span starts with 'Stems' or holds 'spreading'.
example: 'Rhizome 3-5 mm thick' gave rhizome the value thick.

cause: Word endings that hold a count are missing from config/flora_counted_parts.tsv (ridged, sect, partite, cleft, crenate, denticulate, septate, articled, vittate, grooved, branched, paired, French lobé/denté/côtelé/nervé/fasciculé), or a word with its own term is split into a count (2-lobed, 3-lobed, 2-cleft, 1-celled).
remedy: Add rows to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv: ridged -> rib; sect/sected/partite/cleft/fid/forked -> lobe (segment); crenate/serrate/denticulate/denticled/dentate/denté -> tooth (PO:0025518); septate -> septum PO:0000030; articled/articulate/jointed -> fruit segment (mericarp PO_0020075); vittate -> vitta FLOPO_0986042; grooved/sulcate -> groove (hold until a class exists); branched -> branch (inflorescence branch PO:0009081 in an inflorescence); côtelé(e)s -> rib; lobé/lobée/lobés -> lobe; nervé/nervada -> vein; fasciculé(e)s -> flower in a fascicle PO:0025323; paired/pairs of -> collection size 2. Make 'celled' depend on the bearer: locule only for ovary, fruit and anther; elsewhere unicellular/cell. Check whole-word terms before the split: 2-lobed -> bilobed PATO_0002214, 3-lobed -> trilobed PATO_0002241, 2-cleft/2-fid -> bifurcated PATO_0001784, 3-angular -> trigonous FLOPO:0991120, 4-angular -> quadrangular PATO_0001988, 1-cuspidate -> unicuspidate.
detectable: yes: held rows whose span matches \d+(-\d+)?-<suffix> where the suffix is not in the table, or count rows from '2-lobed'/'3-lobed'.
example: 'Fruit 8-10-ridged' was held because 'ridged' has no row.

cause: In sedges, grasses and rushes, 'bladeless (basal) sheaths', 'the lower bladeless', 'reduced to bladeless sheaths' and 'gaines sans limbe' (cataphylls) are read as leaf lamina absent for the whole taxon through rules C350, R0934 and R1884.
remedy: Change rule C350 (collenette_normalization.tsv) and R0934, R1884 (flora_review_rules.tsv): 'bladeless sheath(s)', 'sheaths bladeless', '(sub-)basal/lower/lowest sheaths bladeless', 'lower leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths', 'bladeless sheathed at base', 'sans limbe' in a sheath or culm-base clause -> scale leaf PO_0006003 present at position basal (colours and lustre on the scale leaf), or culm PO:0009047 aphyllopodic FLOPO:0991233. 'bracts bladeless' stays on the bract (hold). Never emit leaf lamina PO_0020039 or leaf PO:0025034 absent from 'bladeless'.
detectable: yes: a lamina- or leaf-absent row whose span holds 'bladeless' or 'sans limbe', especially with 'sheath', or from rule C350/R0934/R1884, or in a taxon with positive lamina rows.
example: 'Basal sheaths bladeless, reddish' became leaf lamina absent for a Carex with blades 2-4 mm wide.

cause: Stage, time, condition and specimen-state cues are missing from config/flora_context_words.tsv, or the wrong row wins ('in bud', 'when mature', 'becoming', 'turning', 'fruiting <part>', 'on seedlings', 'at time of flowering', 'when crushed', 'in/upon drying', 'second year's', 'à l'état jeune/adulte'), so a later or partial state is stated as always true.
remedy: Add rows to config/flora_context_words.tsv: 'in bud'/'in mature bud' -> flower bud stage; 'when mature'/'at maturity'/'when ripe'/'mûr' -> mature PATO_0001701; 'when young'/'à l'état jeune'/'les plus jeunes' -> young PATO_0000309; 'becoming'/'turning'/'fading'/'by morning' -> transition; 'Fruiting <part>' (premodifier), 'persistent <part>' in a fruit paragraph, 'en fruit', 'sous le fruit' -> fruit development stage PO:0001002; 'at (time of) flowering'/'with flowering' -> PO:0007616; 'on seedlings'/'Plantule:'/'premières feuilles' -> seedling stage PO:0007131; 'in drying'/'upon drying'/'à l'état sec'/'sur le sec' -> specimen_condition dried; 'when crushed' -> unscoped for odour; 'second year's' -> old PATO:0000308. Annotator: normalise U+00AD before matching; check specimen_condition before stage; never read degree adverbs or bearer nouns (infructescence, 'flowering branchlets' as a shoot kind) as stages; allow a stage before the noun.
detectable: yes: the span holds one of these phrases but the row has no stage or condition slot, or the row was held as 'stage/process' on a word in this list.
example: 'Calyx green, becoming purple in fruit' gave calyx both green and purple.

cause: French (and some Spanish/Latin) wordings of cues that exist in English are missing: comparisons ('plus long(ue)s/court(e)s/large(s) que', 'dépassant'), relations ('inséré sur', 'adhérent à', 'attaché aux', 'entouré de', 'soudé en tube'), bounds ('jusqu'à', 'atteignant'), per-position counts ('par nœud', 'chaque nœud portant N', 'de chaque côté', 'par aisselle'), regions ('à la base', 'au sommet', 'dans la partie supérieure'), frequency ('parfois', 'souvent'), and habit nouns ('liane').
remedy: For each English cue row add its French forms, with gender and number endings. comparison(): 'plus long(ue)(s)/court(e)(s)/grand(e)(s)/petit(e)(s)/large(s)/étroit(e)(s) que', 'dépassant', 'égalant'. Pattern 09: 'inséré(e)s sur/dans', 's'insérant à l'intérieur de' -> inserted into PATO:0000624; 'adhérent(e)(s) à' -> adherent FLOPO:0991188; 'attaché(e)s à/aux' -> attached to PATO:0001667; 'entouré(e) de', 'inclus dans' -> PATO:0005016; 'soudé(e)s en tube' -> connate FLOPO:0991067. Bounds: 'jusqu'à', 'atteignant' -> inclusive upper bound; 'et parfois plus' -> lower bound. count_position: 'par nœud', 'à chaque nœud', 'chaque nœud (florifère) portant N' -> per_node; 'par aisselle' -> per_axil; 'de chaque côté', 'par côté', 'sur chaque bord' -> each_side. flora_context_words.tsv: 'à la base' -> base, 'au sommet'/'vers le sommet' -> apex, 'dans la partie supérieure/inférieure' -> distal/proximal, 'parfois' -> sometimes, 'le plus souvent' -> usually, 'sub-' prefix -> approximately. Add 'épais de' -> thickness PATO_0000915 and 'carène' -> keel petal PO:0025326.
detectable: yes: held rows from French floras whose span holds one of these strings; list the unmatched French n-grams next to known English cues.
example: 'Étamines plus longues que la corolle' was held: 'plus longues que' is not a comparison cue.

cause: A negated quality or relation of the subject ('not aculeate', 'never palmate', 'not keeled', 'without keels', 'not attached to', 'not concealing', 'not enlarged toward', 'without <adjective> <part>', 'dots absent' on a lamina) is read as absence of the subject or of the part.
remedy: Rule in the negation path: 'not/never <adjective or participle>' negates that quality on the subject; it never yields PATO_0000462 on the subject. 'without/sans <adjective> <part>' negates the adjective on the part (without deciduous X -> X non-deciduous PATO_0001732; sans nervures marquées -> veins inconspicuous PATO_0000464). Surface features that have a quality term give a negated quality on the organ: dots absent/epunctate/without pellucid dots -> punctate PATO_0001512 negated; without keels -> keel-shaped PATO_0002522 negated; ribs absent -> ribbed negated. 'not attached to/free from/not concealing/never borne on X' is a negated relation: no absence and no presence. 'not enlarged toward X' is a negated gradient. If the negated quality does not ground, drop the row.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose span has 'not/never' or 'without' followed by an adjective, participle or verb (it grounds in pato_lexicon or ends in -ed/-ing/-ate), or the absent noun is dots/keel/ribs.
example: 'Stems not aculeate' became stem absent.

cause: Degree, approximation and frequency modifiers on an operand ('sub-', 'slightly', 'broadly', 'narrowly', 'densely', 'markedly', 'shallowly', 'barely', 'mostly', 'usually', 'long-', '-ish') block a union, continuum or plain value match, or are misread as a value, an approximation or a frequency.
remedy: Before pattern 07/08 matching and lexicon lookup, strip a degree-adverb list (slightly, shortly, shallowly, deeply, broadly, narrowly, densely, sparsely, markedly, strongly, distinctly, scarcely, barely, very, très, long-/short-, -ément/-ly adverbs) into an RDF degree on its own operand. Read 'sub-<value>' (including French subaigu and FLOPO values such as subamplexicaul) and '-ish' as the value with value_qualifier approximately (pattern 01), unless a reviewed class exists (subglabrous). 'mostly/largely <relation>' is extent, not frequency. 'densely', 'rich', 'deep', 'bright' are intensity, never approximately. A degree word must not trigger a synonym that implies 'abrupt' (FLOPO:0991316). Keep the degree only on its own operand, not on the whole list.
detectable: yes: held rows that match a reviewed rule or pair once the listed modifiers are stripped, and approximately qualifiers whose cue is not a hedge word.
example: 'Leaves glabrous or sparsely pilose' was held because 'sparsely' blocked the reviewed pair glabrous | pilose.

cause: A general part word ('lobes', 'teeth', 'segments', 'tube', 'rachis', 'branches', 'axis', 'lip', 'thecae', 'spines') is grounded to its default leaf or stem class instead of the matching sub-part of the organ just named or of the container.
remedy: Resolve general part words against the current organ (the clause subject or section heading) before the lexicon default: lobes/teeth/segments after calyx -> calyx lobe FLOPO_0986005, after corolla -> corolla lobe FLOPO_0986006, after perianth -> perianth lobe, after lip/stigma -> lobe of that organ; never leaf lamina lobe PO_0025517 unless the container is a leaf or blade. 'teeth' after exostome/peristome -> peristome tooth PO_0030043. tube after calyx/corolla -> calyx tube / corolla tube FLOPO_0985018. rachis/axis/branches in an inflorescence clause -> inflorescence axis PO_0020122 / inflorescence branch PO_0009081. thecae -> anther theca PO_0009069. 'segments' of a pinnatisect leaf -> leaf lamina lobe. Check: the grounded sub-part must be part_of the container.
detectable: yes: the bearer is a leaf-part class (PO_0025517, leaf rachis, leaf tooth) while the container or preceding organ is a flower part, peristome or inflorescence.
example: 'Corolla ..., lobes 5, ovate' gave the shape to leaf lamina lobe PO_0025517.

cause: Habit nouns (liana, liane(s), climber, vine, twining, creeper, woody/herbaceous climber, arbuste grimpant, trepadora) map to FLOPO growth-form classes without an entity–quality signature (FLOPO_0900035, FLOPO_0985031, FLOPO_0985032, FLOPO_0985034), so they are held at the gate.
remedy: Add habit rows (rule family C354 and Q10-Q14 in flopo2/ingest/ncvc_normalization.tsv), and give the classes EQ signatures: liana/liane/lianes -> whole plant PO:0000003 + climbing FLOPO:0991108 + ligneous PATO:0002348; climber/vine/trepadora/sarmenteux -> whole plant + climbing FLOPO:0991108, with woodiness only from its own word (woody -> ligneous); twining -> stem PO:0009047 + climbing; creeper -> whole plant + creeping FLOPO:0991009; trailer -> procumbent PATO:0002389. Give FLOPO_0900035 the equivalence whole plant and has climbing and ligneous. Size words ('large', 'grande') are separate records or dropped. Block targets that have no EQ axiom.
detectable: yes: any row whose target class has no EQ signature, or whose span holds a habit noun with no grounding.
example: 'Liane jusqu'à 20 m' was held because FLOPO_0900035 has no EQ signature.

cause: A coordinated absence ('A and B absent', 'A, B and C lacking', 'neither A nor B') applies the negation to the last noun only, and the same span gives a 'present' row for another member.
remedy: Use the listed-nouns regex already in absence_scope_problem() to set the negation, not only to check scope: a trailing _ABSENCE_AFTER cue (absent, lacking, wanting, none, 0) and a leading 'neither ... nor' cover every coordinated noun, each grounded as its own absence. Final check before output: never emit present PATO_0000467 from a span that matches _ABSENCE_BEFORE or _ABSENCE_AFTER, and never emit present and absent for one part from one span. A count after joined nouns counts them together and is never given to the last noun alone.
detectable: yes: two rows from the same source span, one present and one absent, or a present row whose span ends in an absence cue.
example: 'Auricles and oral setae absent' gave auricle present and setae absent.

cause: One transcribed row holds several statements: comma-separated characters are merged into one row or one disjunction, shape and size are mixed, a list item is split away from its alternatives, and 'interspersed with' or 'X, sometimes Y' is read as alternatives.
remedy: Transcription prompt: 'Write one row per character and per comma- or semicolon-separated clause. Shape and size are separate rows. An "or" or "to" joins only the values next to it; a value outside it, or with its own qualifier, is a separate row. Keep all alternatives of "A, B, C or D" together in one row, and both ends of "A to B". "interspersed with"/"mixed with" means both are present (two rows). "X, sometimes Y" is X plus Y with frequency sometimes. Never start a row with "or".' Annotator check: reject a span that holds ';' or more than one measurement group.
detectable: yes: a span with ';' or several number groups, a union with operands from different attributes, or a row that starts with 'or'.
example: 'Leaves ovate, 3-5 cm, acuminate' was one row with a disjunction of ovate and acuminate.

cause: The FLOPO GCIs on the direction qualities up (PATO_0000370) and down (PATO_0000365) make sound statements unsatisfiable.
remedy: Remove the up/down GCIs from FLOPO and rerun DeprecateDumbClasses.groovy. Meanwhile, block the lexicon groundings upper/lower -> up/down and map 'facing upwards' on flowers to erect PATO_0000622.
detectable: yes: classes that ELK finds equivalent to owl:Nothing whose definition uses PATO_0000370 or PATO_0000365.
example: 'Radicle pointing down' became unsatisfiable.

cause: Other: single mechanisms with no shared fix. Examples: OCR-glued or line-broken words, scope to one form or locality, statements about distribution, non-plant taxa (lichens), FOC square brackets and '?', a quality on a part declared absent in a stemless taxon, 'in N rows' arrangements, a heterophyllous bearer, and words the transcription changed.
remedy: Case by case. Rejoin line-break hyphens and split OCR-glued tokens when both halves are lexicon words ('ofmidrib'). Skip sentences about one form, locality or distribution ('The form described from ...', 'sporadic in the range'). Filter lichens and other non-plants before annotation, and never fall back to whole plant for a thallus. In FOC, keep a bracketed value only as 'outside range' and a '?' value only as uncertain. In a stemless taxon, send stalk statements to the scape, peduncle or petiole, never to stem. Never put a quality on a part the same taxon states absent. Map heterophyllous to leaf dimorphic FLOPO_0991092. Transcription prompt: copy part and value words exactly as written.
detectable: partly: taxon filter for lichens; '[' or '?' next to a value; tokens not in the lexicon that split into two lexicon words; a quality row on a bearer that has an absence row in the same taxon.
example: A lichen 'thallus' description was annotated on whole plant PO:0000003.
